did_you_know.text: The chapter opens with the declaration “The LORD reigns,” presenting Him as a king clothed in majesty and girded with strength.
According to the verse, the LORD’s reign is connected with the stability of the world: “Indeed, the world is established; it cannot be moved”—the world stands firm and does not collapse.
The LORD’s throne is described as “established”—firm and secure—and it has existed “from of old.” Immediately afterward, the LORD’s eternity is emphasized: “You are from everlasting.”
In the third verse, the rivers are described as raising their voices, giving nature a poetic or proclamatory quality.
The word “raised” is repeated three times in the description of the rivers, emphasizing their power and the noise they create.
The chapter compares the sound of the mighty waters with the crashing waves of the sea, but declares that the LORD is mightier than they are: “The LORD on high is mighty.”
At the end of the chapter, the LORD’s “testimonies” appear, and they are described as “very trustworthy”—reliable and authoritative.
The final verse connects the LORD’s house with holiness: “Holiness befits Your house,” and concludes with the expression “for length of days.”
